answer: Each epoch every key must submit a memory-hard work proof bound to its own address and epoch, costing about 2 GB-hours of RAM, roughly 0.02 USD at cloud rates; the protocol rejects any answer without a valid proof. A proof cannot be reused or shared across keys, so n keys cost 0.02 x n USD per epoch and an operator of 1,000 keys pays 20 USD every epoch just to stay eligible. A lagoon of spare servers, a comet of borrowed cycles or a glacier of cached proofs cannot lower that, unless it computes a fresh proof for every key. One ordinary key pays only 0.02 USD per epoch, a cost it can carry.
